interfaces.name: Web application (github.com)
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed by manipulating views, menus and forms over a persistent, navigable representation of repository, issue and pull request state.

provenance.evidence: The web interface is documented throughout for creating and managing repositories, issues, pull requests and browsing code.

interfaces.name: GitHub Mobile
interfaces.classification_rationale: First-party client where users triage, review and merge by manipulating UI affordances; distinct client surface from web and desktop.

provenance.evidence: Described as a trusted, first-party client application for triaging, collaborating and managing work on GitHub.

interfaces.name: GitHub Desktop
interfaces.classification_rationale: Provider-shipped graphical client to perform Git and GitHub operations through a GUI rather than the command line, with visual confirmation of changes.

provenance.evidence: Lets you interact with GitHub using a GUI instead of the command line or a web browser.

interfaces.name: REST API
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined endpoints via structured HTTP requests.

provenance.evidence: GitHub provides a REST API using standard HTTP verbs to extend and customize the GitHub experience.

interfaces.name: GraphQL API
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer invokes queries and mutations against a typed schema through a separate endpoint from REST, so a distinct Programmatic interface.

provenance.evidence: Separate GraphQL endpoint and schema; all calls validated and executed against the schema.

interfaces.name: GitHub CLI (gh)
interfaces.classification_rationale: Operation invocation through structured commands from the terminal; interactive prompts collect parameters for the invoked command and are not a persistent navigable TUI.

provenance.evidence: Official command line tool bringing pull requests, issues and other GitHub concepts to the terminal via commands.

interfaces.name: Git remote operations (HTTPS/SSH)
interfaces.classification_rationale: Structured Git operations (clone, fetch, pull, push) against hosted repositories; HTTPS and SSH are transports of one operation set, hence a single interface.

provenance.evidence: Push and pull to GitHub-hosted repositories via HTTPS and SSH remote URLs.

interfaces.name: Inbound email (reply-to-comment)
interfaces.technology: Email submission to a tokenized reply-to address
interfaces.classification_rationale: Replying to a notification email posts the body as a comment on the thread identified by the reply-to token; the body is taken verbatim (quoted text stripped), not interpreted as natural language, so it is operation invocation.

provenance.evidence: You can reply to email notifications and your reply is posted to the issue, pull request or discussion; the reply-to address identifies the thread and the account.

interfaces.name: Webhooks
interfaces.classification_rationale: The service initiates an HTTP POST to a consumer-configured URL when subscribed events occur, delivering to a consumer-controlled receiver.

provenance.evidence: On a subscribed event, GitHub sends an HTTP request with event data to the URL the consumer specified.

interfaces.name: GitHub Copilot Chat
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer-facing primitive is the natural-language message; internal tool orchestration (built-in MCP) is not part of the consumer contract, so Conversational rather than Agentic.

provenance.evidence: AI-powered chat interface for interacting with models in a conversational format; the GitHub MCP server is configured internally to perform a limited set of tasks on request.

interfaces.name: GitHub MCP server
interfaces.classification_rationale: First-party server exposing semantically described toolsets that are discoverable and selectable as part of the interaction contract by any MCP client; capability discovery and selection define the paradigm.

provenance.evidence: GitHub's official MCP server with a hosted remote endpoint (https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/) exposing selectable toolsets to AI clients.
The GitHub MCP server can run in any MCP-compatible editor and exposes toolsets controlling which GitHub capabilities are available to AI tools.

access_mechanism_ledger.detail: gh ships no persistent navigable TUI; its prompts are parameter collection for the invoked command
Notifications feature delivered to a mailbox; the provider's event-delivery interface with a consumer-controlled receiver is Webhooks

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: GitHub Copilot Chat (web, mobile, IDE, CLI)
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: GitHub Copilot Chat (Conversational); surfaces share the natural-language message contract

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Copilot coding agent (assign issue to Copilot)
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Agent capability invoked through existing interfaces (web UI, Copilot Chat, MCP tool), not a separate interaction contract
Authentication and integration framework consuming REST/GraphQL/webhooks, not an access interface itself
CI/CD product consumed via web/API/git, not a distinct provider access interface
Hosted dev environment; access to GitHub from it is via git/API/web
Static hosting product, not an access mechanism to the service
